mechanism_narrative: Three consecutive weekly increases in RETAIL_REC from the t-2w trough (-37.3) to t-0w (-34.3) reflect a self-reinforcing recovery in discretionary mobility; absent a shock, this upward momentum persists over the next four weeks, raising the 28-day mean above the prior 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -37.3 at t-2w to -34.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC declines in two or more consecutive weeks during the next four weeks, erasing recent gains, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week rise in WORKPLACES mobility greater than 5 points signals renewed in-office attendance that spills over into higher retail footfall near commute hubs, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -41.6 at t-2w to -33.9 at t-1w, a 7.7 point jump
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC does not increase within the following two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES toward baseline indicates a joint commuting-and-office-return dynamic that compounds to raise retail and recreation visits more than either series alone would predict, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -33.6 to -28.0 while WORKPLACES improved from -41.6 to -34.4 over the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC's 28-day mean does not rise relative to the prior 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In the summer regime, rising PARKS mobility (from 9.4 to 11.9 percent change) indicates increasing outdoor leisure substituting for indoor retail and recreation visits, causing RETAIL_REC growth to stall or decline over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS exceeds 10 percent change from baseline for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from 9.4 at t-3w to 11.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS continues rising above 10 percent while RETAIL_REC also rises concurrently over the next two weeks, the substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility holding near a stable low band (5.4 to 6.0 percent) indicates sustained reduction in home-bound behavior, suggesting people continue spending time away from home, including at retail and recreation venues, over the coming week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed within a narrow 5.4-6.0 band across all four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains stable or falls further but RETAIL_REC declines in the next week, the behavioral linkage hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Stable GROCERY_PHARM percentages (-25.1 to -24.6) indicate no renewed public health restrictions are being imposed on essential retail, implying a permissive policy environment that will not suppress discretionary retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged narrowly between -28.1 and -24.0 across the four weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains stable yet RETAIL_REC's 28-day mean declines relative to the prior 28 days, the policy-stability hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT crosses above -25 percent change from baseline, it signals meaningful transit ridership recovery that enables broader access to retail districts, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above -25 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -33.6 at t-2w to -28.0 at t-0w, approaching the -25 threshold
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses above -25 percent but RETAIL_REC's 28-day mean does not increase relative to the prior 28 days, the threshold hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in PARKS and stable low RESIDENTIAL indicates expanding outdoor and out-of-home activity patterns typical of early summer, which together boost adjacent retail and recreation foot traffic such as outdoor dining and shopping near parks over two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose to 11.9 while RESIDENTIAL held near 5.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS stays elevated and RESIDENTIAL stays low but RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next two weeks, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.
